lines.trans: What is this box? Let me carry it out to the parking lot for you.
Cindy's fans say they love me now!
Senior, did that blind-date guy from lunchtime happen to call yet? If he calls, will you meet him?
As the saying goes, it takes a man to read a man—and from another man's eyes, he sounds rather questionable.
What could you possibly know about someone you have never even laid eyes on?
He said he likes fierce women, yet rather than fierce, you have clear convictions, call out what is wrong, and fight what needs fighting…
That is the exact definition of fierce, Seung-chan!
Plus he said he likes stylish women, and I dislike men who judge women mainly on appearances.
Did you not like Hye-joo because she was pretty? Wait—are you worried I will date just any guy out of anger at Joon-mo?
Who knows, maybe I might do just that.
You must not!

Goodbye! (go safely)

meanings.note: Used as honorific polite imperative (가세요!).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (go safely)
Let us do that (go (honorific)) right away.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.
Did you hear about this that person?
I was busy today because of that person.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 아나운서는 아니잖아, 굳이 따지자면 일반인에 가깝지!
examples.trans: I am not an announcer—strictly speaking, I am closer to an ordinary citizen!
This expression comes from 'strictly speaking'.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Common verb for expressing thoughts in words.

examples.trans: Please speak slowly.
Speak loudly.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Did you hear about this not fond of?
I was busy today because of not fond of.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
Test
Test2
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.
It really is strongly, boldly compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is strongly, boldly and nice.

meanings.note: Used as noun (소개팅).

examples.text: 선배, 혹시 아까 점심때 말한 소개팅 전화 왔습니까? 오면 만나실 겁니까?
examples.trans: Senior, did that blind-date guy from lunchtime happen to call yet? If he calls, will you meet him?
This point about blind-date is really important.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.note: Used as loanword adnominal (스타일리시한).

examples.text: 너처럼 스타일리시한 여자가 좋대, 너 옷 잘 입잖아!
examples.trans: He also likes stylish women like you—you dress great!

examples.text: 그리고 스타일리시한 여자를 좋아한다고 했는데 외모 위주로 판단하는 분은 별로라고 생각합니다.
examples.trans: Plus he said he likes stylish women, and I dislike men who judge women mainly on appearances.

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.en: to fight; to quarrel; to argue
meanings.note: The opponent takes -와/과 or -랑.

examples.trans: Do you fight with your younger sibling often?
Don't fight with each other and get along.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Usually followed by a negative verb to mean 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

examples.trans: Nobody is here.
Please give me anything.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

examples.text: 내가 열받아서 그냥 나오지 마라 그랬더니 진짜 안 나오려나 봐.
examples.trans: I lost my temper and told her not to come out, and now she really might skip it.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 열받다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (lost my temper and).

meanings.note: colloquially often pronounced/written 이쁘다

examples.trans: The flowers are really pretty.
This color is prettier.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Used as noun (외모).

examples.text: 그리고 스타일리시한 여자를 좋아한다고 했는데 외모 위주로 판단하는 분은 별로라고 생각합니다.
examples.trans: Plus he said he likes stylish women, and I dislike men who judge women mainly on appearances.
This point about outward looks is really important.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예진이가 먹고 싶은 거 위주로 시켰구먼, 걔가 산낙지 킬러거든.
examples.trans: Ye-jin clearly ordered all her own favorites—she is crazy about live octopus.
Here the word for 'mainly around' is key.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?
Please look at this.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (자기주장).

examples.text: 그분이 센 여자를 좋아한다고 했는데 선배는 세다기보다는 자기주장 확실하고 따질 거 따지고 싸울 거 싸우고…
examples.trans: He said he likes fierce women, yet rather than fierce, you have clear convictions, call out what is wrong, and fight what needs fighting…
This point about one's own convictions is really important.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.

meanings.note: Compound of lunch and time.

examples.trans: Let's meet at lunchtime.
Lunchtime has passed.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

meanings.en: to like, to be fond of
meanings.note: Takes an object marked with 을/를.

examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?
I like listening to music.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Here the word for 'from the parking lot' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: On what grounds did you reach that conclusion?
This expression comes from 'did you judge?'.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'fan', used for admirers of singers, actors, or sports teams.

examples.trans: I'm a longtime fan of Cindy.
Fans are waiting in front of the waiting room.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Softens a question or expresses uncertainty.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
Do you happen to have time?

확실하다.gloss: to be certain, to be clear

meanings.en: to be certain, to be sure, to be clear
meanings.note: Sino-Korean adjective.

examples.trans: Are you sure?
clear evidence

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -에 (홧김에).

examples.text: 너 혜주 예뻐서 좋아했다면서? 아 뭐야, 내가 준모 때문에 열받아서 홧김에 아무 남자나 만나고 다닐까 봐?
examples.trans: Did you not like Hye-joo because she was pretty? Wait—are you worried I will date just any guy out of anger at Joon-mo?
This point about in a fit of pique is really important.
